questions.question: A woman remembered as a courtesan of Lurkee Mahil took up the role of a warrior and strategist during the Revolt of 1857, helping a rebel cavalry unit operating out of Kanpur. In which city was she born, and by what other name was she also known?
questions.rationale: Only this paragraph gives Azizun Nisa's birthplace and alternate name; both are verbatim, distinctive, and absent from the question.

questions.question: A writer arguing that no part of humanity could be written off — militarily, ideologically, or morally — invoked both Abraham Lincoln's warning that no nation could remain half slave and half free, and the words of an English poet on human interconnectedness, in a shrinking world. Name the poet.
questions.rationale: The paragraph names John Donne as the poet invoked alongside the Lincoln reference; the question describes the argument without naming the poet, author, or work.

questions.question: A lecturer, thanking a mentor whose guidance had nurtured 'this Centre' into what it had become, proposed an alternative title for his talk on the worldwide retreat of socialism — a Persian-language phrase likening the departure of heresy from the Kaaba to what would remain of the faith. What was that alternative title, in full?
questions.rationale: The Persian alternative title is a one-off phrase in the corpus; its distinctive transliterated words serve as the needle since no other names appear in the paragraph.

questions.question: In 1851, an Indian reformer and his colleagues founded both a Zoroastrian reform society and a Gujarati-language newspaper that campaigned against child marriage and the practice of nautches. Name the newspaper and the society.
questions.rationale: Both organisation names are verbatim, distinctive, and given only in this paragraph; the question withholds Naoroji's name.

questions.question: In discussing India's economic decline under colonial rule, a social reformer credited two Indian judges, alongside Dadabhai Naoroji, with devising ways to stimulate the country's industries and commerce without violating the laws of economics. Name the two judges.
questions.rationale: The two judges are named only alongside Naoroji in this paragraph; the question uses Naoroji (not the subject of this piece) as the findable anchor while withholding Agarkar's name.

questions.question: A Marathi social reformer's book contrasting communalism in India with the medieval history of Europe traces the Arab invasion of Europe through Gibraltar in 711 CE, noting that Arab forces reached a city in France within 21 years, before a Christian pushback was completed with the fall of a certain city in 1492. Name the book, and the city whose fall in 1492 completed that reconquest.
questions.rationale: The book title and the fall of Granada in 1492 are the two checkable facts unique to this paragraph; the question omits Hamid Dalwai's name and the organisation named in the title.

questions.question: An article on India's planning debates blames two clusters of Western economists for keeping Indian universities wedded to outmoded dirigiste doctrines — one cluster of 'pronounced left-wingers.' Name two of the four economists in that left-wing cluster.
questions.rationale: The named economist clusters occur only in this paragraph; the question withholds the author's name (BR Shenoy) and the article title.

questions.question: A social reformer from a Brahmin family nonetheless criticised the upper-class attitudes of Brahmins in his writings, and produced several plays skewering Brahmin priests, including one in 1886 dramatizing a devotee king's story, and another in 1889. Name these two plays.
questions.rationale: The two play titles with their years are given only in this paragraph; the question withholds Veeresalingam's name.

questions.question: India's long tradition of dissent, reaching back to disputes between the brahman and shraman (nastik) traditions, is said to find an echo in the works of a certain ancient writer, in the Ashokan inscriptions, and in the writings of a medieval scholar who described a counter religion of the Shramanas. Name these two writers.
questions.rationale: Megasthenes and Al Beruni are named together only in this paragraph; the question avoids reproducing the four-word article title.

questions.question: During an incident at Checkpoint Charlie, a man lay mortally wounded for about half an hour, moaning for help, before he died, while American troops held back from giving him medical aid for fear of the consequences — an episode said to have exposed the weakness of the Western position in Berlin. Name the man who died at Checkpoint Charlie.
questions.rationale: Fechter's surname is the one distinctive, verbatim fact this paragraph supplies, and it is withheld from the question itself.
